mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the last month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strong consumer demand, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases over the past two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE is above 8% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter indicates strong economic growth, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 increases over the past quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the last month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases by more than 1% within the last month.
